messages:
ops-bot: Paging: RUNTIME_CANARY_HIGH_LATENCY triggered for rdx-canary-3 (region: us-west-2). 90th p50->p95 jump observed in the last 3m, error rate +4%. Auto-notify to #incidents and oncall. thread_ts=1798054321

sam: ack — oncall here, grabbing it. Any recent deploys?

nora: I pushed the canary rollout at 17:12 (deploy id: deploy-20260315-17:12). Small config change: default batching policy now uses dynamic windowing from the new batching lib.

lee: seeing kernel fallback messages in the canary logs — lots of lines like: `WARN runtime: falling back to generic kernel for matmul, reason: kernel init failed (unsupported q8 op)` — latency ballooned after fallback.

jane: customer CS reported a spike in slow responses for a few large customers (session ids shared in DM). One enterprise has ~5% 500s for generation requests. Notified them that we're investigating.

sam: OK confirmed: fallback + batching change together explains it. New batching lib increases request coalescing window which, combined with kernel fallback stalls, increases tail latency. Evidence: request queues growing in canary pods and concurrency hitting 1.5x expected.

nora: rolling back batching change on canary now. Command: ```./deploy rollback-config --env=canary --config=batching_dynamic_v2```

ops-bot: deploy job started: rollback-config for rdx-canary-3 (job 9821).

lee: also trying to force-reload optimized kernels on the affected nodes — running `supervisorctl restart runtime-worker` on rdx-canary-3-*/instance. Might be that a kernel compile failed during deploy and left the worker in fallback state.

sam: if rollback-config doesn't restore tail latency within 5m we should flip the canary kill-switch and roll the canary back to previous image. Use admin-console -> rollouts -> canary -> revert to image digest `sha256:ab12...`

nora: rollback-config completed. Metrics show p95 dropping slowly but still elevated (was 1.4s, now 900ms). Kernel fallback log rate has reduced but not gone away.

lee: evidence that one kernel binary failed to load due to a packaging path mismatch — copying corrected kernel blob to nodes now and restarting runtime-worker.

jane: customer-updates: sent a short note to the affected customer group: "We observed increased latency on canary after a recent change. We're rolling back and applying fixes. No action required on your side; will update shortly."

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-27. Severity: P2. Summary: runtime canary latency regression after deploy due to kernel fallback + batching config.

sam: After the kernel blob restore + worker restart, p95 is back to baseline for 6 of 8 canary pods. Two pods still show intermittent fallback; I'm draining them and forcing redeploy. Command: `kubectl drain pod/rdx-canary-3-45 && kubectl delete pod/rdx-canary-3-45`

nora: I am toggling the canary kill-switch flag briefly to stop further traffic to the canary pool while we stabilize: `feature_flags.set('canary_accept_traffic', false)`

ops-bot: Feature flag update accepted. canary_accept_traffic=false for rdx-canary-3. Traffic is re-routed to stable pool.

lee: redeploy of problem pods complete, kernel load checks ok (`kernel_version: v2.3.1, status: loaded`). No fallback logs on new pods.

sam: Monitoring: error rate back to baseline, p95 at expected values. I'm going to keep the kill-switch engaged for 20 more minutes then gradually re-enable traffic after confirming stable behavior.

jane: CS confirmed affected enterprise saw recovery and reduced 500s after we re-routed. They asked for RCA and ETA for stable rollout; told them we'll follow up after postmortem.

incident-bot: Update INC-20260315-27: urgent mitigation performed — config rollback, kernel blob fix, pod redeploys, temporary canary kill-switch. Current status: degraded -> recovering.

sam: Postmortem action items (quick list): 1) Add pre-deploy kernel-load check to CI for packaging mismatch. 2) Add a short-circuit check in the batching lib to avoid increasing window when kernel fallback detected. 3) Improve canary kill-switch automation to drain pods automatically. 4) Customer comms template for canary regressions. Assigning owners in thread.

nora: assigning myself to item 1 and 2. I'll open PRs today.

lee: I'll take item 3 (ops automation).

jane: I'll own item 4 and draft the template.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-27: status -> monitoring. Incident will be routed to postmortems channel after 24h if no regression.

sam: thanks team. Leaving follow-up tasks in tracker and linking to this thread. If anyone sees new spikes reopen the page.

ops-bot: Note: oncall handoff in 20m to @nora -> @lee. Ensure clocked handover in #eng-oncall.
